# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Sawyer Iverson**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Ambetter — Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 10, 2026**
- **Member:** Sawyer Iverson
- **Member ID:** W437498644
- **Reference number:** POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270
- **Denied service:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- **Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), State of Tennessee
- **Requesting surgeon:** Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery

---

## A note on the policy being applied

I want to be clear at the outset about what I have and have not been given. The denial notice dated August 10, 2026 states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not name that policy, and no criteria document or criteria text has been provided to me. **I am therefore not quoting any plan policy language in this letter, because the plan has not given me any to quote.** Everything below is drawn from my own medical records. I ask that my appeal be read with that in mind, and I am requesting the criteria in writing (see the section below) so that I can respond to the actual standard being applied to me.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296, and I am asking Ambetter to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. The stated reason for the denial was that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Reyes, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed. In this letter I am setting out, point by point, the clinical record that exists in my chart, so that the file in front of the reviewer is complete.

## The clinical record

The following facts are documented in the prior authorization packet and my medical records:

**Duration and course of symptoms.** I have had 12 months of progressive pain in the foot. The pain is not relieved by rest.

**Non-surgical treatment I have already completed.** I completed 16 weeks of conservative care, from March 20, 2026 through July 10, 2026, consisting of activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic. I attended 20 visits. This course of care is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication and injection.** I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief. I received a corticosteroid injection on May 25, 2026, which gave me only about 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken on June 29, 2026 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.

**Physical examination.** Provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

**Functional impact.** I cannot tolerate closed shoes. There is ulceration risk over the bony prominence.

**Surgical candidacy.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker.

## Why this record answers the reason given for the denial

The denial was not based on a finding that I fail any particular clinical threshold. It was based on the documentation being considered incomplete. That is a documentation determination, and it is answered by documentation.

The record above contains a measured symptom duration, a dated and quantified course of conservative treatment with a specific number of visits and a source note, a documented medication trial and its outcome, a documented injection and the duration of relief it provided, dated weight-bearing radiographs with measured angles, objective examination findings, a described functional limitation, and the clinical factors relevant to whether I can safely undergo surgery. My treating orthopedic surgeon has reviewed all of this and has documented that the procedure is needed.

I recognize that Ambetter may apply specific numerical thresholds — for example, a required duration of conservative care or a required angle measurement. I cannot address those thresholds, because none has been stated to me and no criteria text has been provided. What I can say is that my chart reports the actual measured values above, and I am asking that they be compared against the plan's real criteria rather than against a finding that they are absent. If any single item is still considered missing, I ask that the plan identify that item specifically by name so that my surgeon's office can supply it, rather than denying the request as a whole.

## Written request for the criteria applied to my case

**I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or other criterion that Ambetter relied on to deny this request.** I understand that my plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. I am specifically asking for **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with the identity and clinical specialty of the reviewer who made the decision. Federal ACA and ERISA appeal rules entitle me to the specific criterion relied upon for an adverse benefit determination. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. Without them, I am being asked to prove that my documentation satisfies a standard I have never been shown. Please provide the criteria text with, or before, the response to this appeal so that I have a meaningful opportunity to respond to it.

## Closing request

I am asking Ambetter to overturn the denial dated August 10, 2026 (reference number POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270) and to authorize bunion surgery, CPT 28296, as requested by Reyes, MD. If the plan maintains the denial, I am asking for a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion I am found not to meet, identifies the specific documentation still considered missing, and explains my further appeal rights, including external review.

Per the denial notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of that notice — **by February 6, 2027** — and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand that Ambetter/Centene administers appeals by state, and that I may also file using the Tennessee appeal or grievance form available at ambetterhealth.com by selecting my state, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if anything further is needed. My surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone] and I authorize Ambetter to obtain any additional records directly from Reyes, MD. I would appreciate written confirmation that this appeal has been received.

Thank you for taking a second look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Sawyer Iverson**
Member ID: W437498644
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-10]; [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-20 to 2026-07-10]; [Weight-bearing radiograph report, 2026-06-29]; [Office notes from Reyes, MD]; [Injection record, 2026-05-25]; [Other records enclosed]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
